subject: ILCE-6400 updater and service trust boundary

observations.claim: Across the outer updater and 29 embedded PE components, no firmware-verification import or allowlisted public-key marker was found; the only Crypt32 calls are DPAPI protection functions in the MFC runtime.
The custom updater shell has bodies only through CXD90014, while CXD90045 supports historical decryption but its encryption method explicitly raises an unsupported error.

Command 0x10 starts with an empty handshake, sends only the first negotiated FDAT chunk, and may return success before EOF; after the mode switch and updater-device reconnect, the host seeks back to the FDAT start and resends the complete payload through command 0x40.
Service mode is a separate authenticated protocol with file and memory reads, but the same implementation also exposes mutating operations that this acquisition design explicitly denies.

inferences.claim: The normal-runtime guard validates header identity fields, while any full-payload authenticity decision must occur later in the separate updater-mode environment because the Windows host does not expose a located verifier.

inferences.source: service-mode source and public alpha 6400 report
inferences.claim: A read-only service-mode acquisition is a more direct route to authenticated target firmware evidence than attempting to manufacture a signed generation-four updater.

unresolved.claim: The camera-resident verifier implementation, public trust anchor, signed byte range, and exact mapping from verification failure to protocol status remain unlocated.
No alpha 6400 identity, partition metadata, boot ROM, filesystem file, or flash image has been acquired through the proposed read-only service path.
The alpha 6400 UI, touch dispatch, color tables, module ABI, and boot-time integrity controls cannot be mapped until authenticated target contents are available.

conclusion: The Windows updater does not expose a located firmware-signature bypass, and the historical updater shell cannot generate a CXD90045 image. The next viable evidence step is a tightly allowlisted, read-only alpha 6400 service acquisition; it is not an install or a bypass.
